answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces cryptographic stake burning where creating n identities scales at superlinear quadratic cost, O(n²). When validating tasks, each agent deposits a stake that is irreversibly burned upon malicious divergence. Like a shifting dune swallowing duplicates, this friction destroys attacker capital. Even if an adversary generates a synthetic sonnet or violet pattern across clones, exponential stake requirements make mass coordination mathematically unprofitable.
